title: AI Tools Schema
description: Tool definitions for the AI harness in OpenAI-compatible format

function.name: search
function.description: Search the web for information. Use this when you need to find current information, facts, or answers that you don't already know. Returns top 3 results with title, URL, content, and relevance score.

query.description: The search query to look up on the web

function.name: code_execution
function.description: Execute JavaScript code in a secure sandbox environment. Use this when the user wants to create, modify, or manage channel resources like commands, triggers, rewards, or events. The code has access to the channel's API through the provided environment variables.

code.description: The JavaScript code to execute. Can use 'await' for async operations. Use 'fetch' for API calls. Return a result object.

request.description: What the user is asking the code to do - used for context if code needs to make decisions

function.name: AST_PARSER
function.description: Execute bot commands using AST syntax. Use this to perform moderation actions (ban, timeout, vip), channel management (set.title, set.game), or other bot operations. The channel ID is automatically provided by the system. If you are not 100% sure of a command's exact syntax or arguments, call ast_docs FIRST to look it up. Examples: 'ban username 300', 'set.title New Stream Title', 'add.vip username', 'clear.chat'

command.description: The AST command to execute. Do NOT include the $() wrapper - just the command name and arguments. Examples: 'ban offensiveuser 300', 'set.title Watch my new stream', 'add.vip gooduser', 'clear.chat'

userlevel.description: Requested permission level: 7 for mod actions (ban, vip, clear.chat), 8 for broadcaster actions (set.title, set.game, add.mod). The system clamps this to the requesting chatter's actual permission level, so never claim a level above what the chatter has.

function.name: ast_docs
function.description: Look up the bot's AST command catalog. Returns the exact syntax, arguments, and examples for commands. Use BEFORE calling AST_PARSER whenever a command takes multiple or structured arguments, whenever you are unsure of the exact format, or when checking if a command exists for what the user wants. Read-only and safe to call. Search by function name ('start.poll') or by intent ('start a vote in chat').

query.description: Function name ('start.poll', 'tts.clone') or natural-language intent ('ban a user for 10 minutes', 'start a prediction').

surface.description: Optional. 'action' (default) for things the bot executes in chat; 'authoring' for functions used inside command/reward message templates (counters, event data, string helpers).

limit.description: Optional max number of matches (1-10, default 3).

function.name: chat_summary
function.description: Get the most recent chat messages to summarize recent chat activity. Use when a mod or the streamer asks what happened in chat, what they missed, or what users have been talking about.

count.description: How many recent messages to include (capped by plan tier).

function.name: stream_stats
function.description: Get live stream session metrics: uptime, current/average/peak viewers, follows, subs, bits, chat messages and commands used. Use when the streamer or mods ask how the stream is going.

function.name: create_memory
function.description: Save important information to memory for future reference. Use when you learn something about the channel, streamer preferences, user facts, or when told to remember or avoid something. The AI will confirm if saved or indicate pending review.

type.description: Type of memory - boundary=don't do something, preference=streamer likes/dislikes, known_user_fact=user info, channel_lore=important events, running_joke=recurring jokes

content.description: Detailed description of what to remember

summary.description: Short summary (under 100 chars) for quick reference

username.description: Only for a fact about the current chatter. Never provide another user's username; the system binds user facts to the verified current chatter identity.
